items.title: U.N. Updates: Zelensky Warns of Growing Global Cost of Russia’s War in Ukraine
items.summary: Ukraine’s president said rising fuel prices and deadlier drone technology showed that the fighting have spilled beyond his country’s borders. He called for steps to end to the war before winter.

items.title: Tigrayan Forces Mobilize Against the Central Government in Ethiopia
items.summary: Tigray People’s Liberation Front seized a key airport in the city of Mekelle, as fears grow of a possible return to a full-scale war.

items.title: Trump’s New Favorite Neighbor: Mexico
items.summary: President Trump built his political brand in part on bashing Mexico. Now his second presidency depends on deepening partnerships with the country.

items.title: India’s Election Panel Faces New Scrutiny Over Voter Roll Revisions
items.summary: An explosive news report says election commission members objected to the measures that excluded millions of people from voting, which critics say favor the government.

items.title: Ancient Wall Found in Paris Provides Clues to City’s Origins
items.summary: A discovery at a Parisian hospital, on an island in the Seine, has given archaeologists clues about the city as Julius Caesar may have found it.

items.title: How China’s Leader Plans to Win the Future With A.I.
items.summary: A decade ago, Xi Jinping asked if China could master A.I. His push is remaking the economy, challenging the United States and keeping society under control.

items.title: Why Germany’s Leader Merz Is Struggling to Sway Voters
items.summary: As the far right surges, Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s unpopular economic policies and gruff manner have failed to sway voters turned by rivals’ promises of easy fixes.

items.title: The Winner of This Rivalry Gets Ice Cream. But So Does the Loser.
items.summary: The competition between two popular ice cream shops in Ramallah inspires fierce loyalties, and a running joke, for lovers of cones piled high with flavors.

items.title: U.S. Rebukes Australia Over Proposed Limits on Social Media Algorithms
items.summary: The U.S. Embassy said a draft law allowing users to opt out of systems that choose what they can see in their feeds could amount to censorship.

items.title: Youth Frustration and Migration Shadow Morocco’s Election
items.summary: Unemployment and poor public services fueled the border crisis at Ceuta and Gen Z protests, but frustrated young people may stay away from the polls.

items.title: Epstein’s Accountant and Lawyer Are Said to Be Under Federal Investigation
items.summary: Lawyers for Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn said their clients were “confident that any investigation will reveal that they were not involved in any of Epstein’s crimes.”

items.title: NBC, CBS and More TV Networks Didn’t Film Xi’s Arrival Amid Trump’s Press Ban
items.summary: The White House TV pool has suspended its coverage of President Trump since he banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

items.title: Judge Holds Off on Immediate Ruling on White House’s Media Ban
items.summary: Judge Timothy J. Kelly heard arguments about President Trump’s recent decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds. He said he would issue a decision about it “as soon as possible.”

items.title: Trump Backtracks on Plan for New Controls on N.I.H. Grants
items.summary: Democrats and Republicans in Congress opposed the creation of a commission with the power to veto federal research awards.

items.title: The New York Times stopped publishing White House pool photos in support of the banned outlets.
The judge in this case once restored White House access for a CNN reporter after Trump stripped it.
Florida Files Lawsuit Against The New York Times
items.summary: The state’s attorney general demanded access to company records to examine how the newspaper’s board oversees editorial standards amid claims of anti-Israel bias.

items.title: Here’s what the news outlets and the White House have said in court papers.
Bond Yields Soar as Investors Foresee Another Fed Interest Rate Increase
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield on Wednesday rose to around 5.1 percent, as investors increasingly expect the Fed Reserve will raise interest rates again.

items.title: Trump faced the sting of cancellation this week.
Meta Unveils 3 Smart Glasses With Built-In A.I.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence again dominated the company’s annual developer conference, as Mark Zuckerberg doubled down on how the technology can empower people.

items.title: I Gave My Life Over to Meta’s A.I. Agent and Was Blown Away
items.summary: Muse, Meta’s A.I. agent, helped handle my dental insurance, booked dinner reservations and created a podcast for me. It also required my most personal data, and trust.

items.title: America’s A.I. Leaders Warn U.N. of Possible Peril Absent a Global Response
items.summary: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic told the Security Council that international cooperation was needed to ensure that A.I. remains under human control.

items.title: An A.I. Image of Trump Kissing a Woman Was Fake. It Spread Anyway.
items.summary: Advances in artificial intelligence and the myriad ways content is shared online have made establishing authenticity even more difficult for users of social media.

items.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Tried Breaching Four Other Targets, With No Prompting
items.summary: In each incident, the technology appeared to be conducting mundane data collection and resorted to hacking techniques to get it, researchers said.

items.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators
items.summary: New Jersey officials said that the natural gas-powered generators, each the size of a tractor-trailer, were operating without permits.

items.title: Where Is the U.S. Beating China on A.I., and Where Is It Lagging?
items.summary: As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, his country lags behind the United States on A.I. development in key areas — but Beijing has advantages elsewhere.

items.title: Gerard Barron, Metals Company Chief, Makes the Case for Seafloor Mining
items.summary: The head of the company hoping to become the first to conduct commercial deep-sea mining said mines on land had a much larger environmental footprint.

items.title: Anthropic Releases a New A.I. Model, Opus 5.5, Amid Safety Debate
items.summary: The company released a cheaper, faster model that it said was the strongest performer on its most rigorous internal safety tests to date.

items.title: An Army of Paid Creators Is Carpeting the Web With Political Content
items.summary: Unlike celebrity influencers with large followings, these creators produce a blizzard of videos for a fraction of the cost of traditional online campaigns and, in the process, shift public conversation.
